<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Song of Songs 2:16">Targ. Cant. II, 16</cite>.—
M. Kat. 17ᵃ מאי ש׳ what is (the etymology of) shamta? Rab said שׁם̇ מ̇ית̇ה there is death; Samuel said, שְׁמָמָה יהיה (Ms. M. שַׁמָּה; Ar. שם תהא, read: שמה תהא) he shall be (be thou) a desolation.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 17a:24">Ib.</cite> <he>ליהוי האי גברא בש׳</he> that man (thou) be excommunicated. Ib. 16ᵃ <he>לא חל ש׳ עליה וכ׳</he> (masc.) the ban has not yet rested on him thirty days. Ib. <he>עד דחיילא ש׳ וכ׳</he> (it cannot be raised) before he has been under the ban thirty days.
<cite ref="Sotah 5a:16">Sot. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>בש׳ דאית ביה ובש׳ דלית ביה</he> he (the scholar) in whom there is pride deserves excommunication, and also he in whom there is no pride at all.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 12b:8">Kidd. 12ᵇ</cite> Rab ordered to be lashed <he>על דחלא ש׳ וכ׳</he> him who allowed excommunication (for contempt of court) to rest on him thirty days (and did not submit to authority).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 70a:9">B. Mets. 70ᵃ</cite> <he>ולא מקבל עליה ש׳ דרבנ</he>‌<he>ן</he> Ms. M. and does not bring upon himself the ban of the Rabbis (but obeys their summons); a. fr.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 13:18">Targ. Y. Deut. XIII, 18</cite>.—Pl. <he>שַׁמְתִּין</he>.
